TOP NEWS

LLMs

GOOGLE UNVEILS GEMINI 2.0 MODELS, NOW SUPPORTING LARGE-SCALE
PRODUCTION TASKS WITH MULTIMODAL REASONING

⇧ 16,485 Likes

		 [5] 

WHAT'S NEW

Google makes Gemini 2.0 Flash generally available and introduces
Flash-Lite and Pro Experimental. These models expand context windows,
enhance multimodal reasoning, and improve coding capabilities. 

MODEL OVERVIEW

 	* 2.0 FLASH (GENERAL ACCESS):  It can handle real-time,
large-scale production tasks with 1 million tokens. You can apply it
to tasks requiring high-frequency text generation, multimodal data,
and reasoning.

 	* 2.0 FLASH-LITE (PUBLIC PREVIEW): It optimizes cost without
sacrificing speed. It generates one-line captions for 40,000 images
for under $1 in AI Studio’s paid tier.

 	* 2.0 PRO EXPERIMENTAL: You can run complex reasoning and coding
tasks using a 2-million-token context window. Analyze large documents,
generate complex code, and call external tools like Google Search.

PERFORMANCE

 	* The models can handle multimodal data with large context windows:
1 million tokens in Flash and Flash-Lite, 2 million tokens in Pro
Experimental.

 	* Gemini 2.0 outperforms 1.5 Pro on tasks like general knowledge,
multilingual understanding, and code generation.

 	* It achieves cost-efficient output with Flash-Lite, which delivers
higher quality than 1.5 Flash without increasing cost or latency.

HOW GEMINI 2.0 COMPARES TO ITS PREVIOUS MODELS?
Gemini 2.0 models improve over the 1.5 series in efficiency, speed,
and quality. 2.0 FLASH IS FASTER AND HIGHER QUALITY THAN 1.5 PRO,
optimized for large-scale, high-frequency tasks. 2.0 FLASH-LITE
OUTPERFORMS 1.5 FLASH while maintaining the same cost and speed. 2.0
PRO EXPERIMENTAL EXPANDS THE CONTEXT WINDOW TO 2 MILLION TOKENS,
doubling 1.5 Pro’s limit, and enhances coding performance with
better reasoning and tool integration.

ACCESS AND AVAILABILITY

 	* GEMINI 2.0 FLASH is GENERALLY AVAILABLE via the Gemini API in
Google AI Studio and Vertex AI.

 	* GEMINI 2.0 FLASH-LITE is in PUBLIC PREVIEW in Google AI Studio and
Vertex AI.

 	* GEMINI 2.0 PRO EXPERIMENTAL is available in GOOGLE AI STUDIO,
VERTEX AI, AND THE GEMINI APP for Gemini Advanced users.

 	* 2.0 FLASH THINKING EXPERIMENTAL is accessible in the GEMINI APP on
desktop and mobile.

 	* You can integrate these models into PRODUCTION APPLICATIONS using
the Gemini API.

TOP LECTURES

LLMs

HOW TRANSFORMER LLMS WORK [12]

⇧ 1,154 Likes

This lecture is presented by Jay Alammar and Maarten Grootendorst, the
authors of the book Hands-On Large Language Models. Here, learn how
transformer LLMs process text through tokenization, embeddings,
attention mechanisms, and transformer blocks. Understand recent
improvements like KV cache, multi-query attention, and
Mixture-of-Experts (MoE). Explore key components and their
implementation in Hugging Face, and enhance your ability to build and
analyze LLM-based applications.

Agents

CHOOSING THE RIGHT AI AGENT FRAMEWORK [13]

⇧ 841 Likes

Learn about autonomous agents and how they differ from AI pipelines
and standalone LLMs. Explore three popular frameworks—LangGraph,
CrewAI, and OpenAI Swarm—through a hands-on Agentic Finance App
example. Understand when to use each framework, and get a preview of
debugging and observability topics in Part II.

Hardware Optimization

HOW TO SCALE YOUR MODEL [14]

⇧ 1,536 Likes

Learn how to scale LLMs on TPUs by understanding hardware limitations,
parallelism, and efficient training techniques. Explore how to
estimate training costs, memory needs, and optimize performance using
strategies like data, tensor, pipeline, and expert parallelism. Gain
hands-on experience with LLaMA-3, and learn to profile and debug your
code.

DEEP DIVE

Agent

BUILDING RELIABLE AI AGENTS: A STEP-BY-STEP GUIDE

AI agents process information, make decisions, and complete tasks in
applications like chatbots and research tools. A well-designed agent
requires a suitable LLM, structured control logic, and clear
instructions. Here’s a step-by-step guide:

CHOOSE THE RIGHT LLM

Not all LLMs perform equally. Select one that excels in reasoning,
supports chain-of-thought (CoT) prompting, and delivers consistent
responses. Experiment with models and refine prompts for better
results.

DEFINE THE AGENT’S CONTROL LOGIC

Decide how your agent makes decisions:

 	* TOOL USE – Calls tools when needed, responds otherwise.
 	* REFLECTION – Generates, critiques, and refines responses.
 	* REACT – Plans, executes, observes, and iterates.
 	* PLAN-THEN-EXECUTE – Outlines steps before execution.

SET CORE INSTRUCTIONS & FEATURES

Define how the agent handles unclear queries, formats responses, and
interacts with users. Clear system prompts ensure consistent behavior.

IMPLEMENT A MEMORY STRATEGY

Use a sliding window for short-term memory, summaries for recall, or
long-term storage for personalization.

EQUIP THE AGENT WITH TOOLS & APIS

Define tool names, functions, input/output formats, and error handling
to extend capabilities.

CLARIFY THE AGENT’S ROLE & TASKS

A well-scoped agent performs better. Specify its mission, tasks, and
limitations.

HANDLE RAW LLM OUTPUTS

Post-process responses into structured formats, validate correctness,
and ensure proper tool execution.

SCALE TO MULTI-AGENT SYSTEMS

For complex workflows, manage inter-agent communication, error
handling, and task coordination. Example: One agent fetches data,
another summarizes, and a third generates a report.
